newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran envoy expects talks with UAE on islands soon.
newsitem.headline: Iran envoy expects talks with UAE on islands soon.

text.p: Iran's new ambassador to the United Arab Emirates said in remarks published on Saturday that Tehran was about to launch a new round of talks with the UAE to resolve a dispute over three Gulf islands.

Hussein Sadiqi, who until his appointment as envoy to Abu Dhabi was Iran's chief negotiator in talks with the UAE over the islands of Greater Tunb, Lesser Tunb and Abu Musa, said talks were the only way to settle the row peacefully.
"We are about to start a new round of talks," he told the Saudi Arabian newspaper Asharq al-Awsat.
"I believe that if these talks intensify and take their normal course away from interference by others, we will be able to reach the needed harmony," he added.
"But this needs patience and some time...and we should not respond to any outside interference," he added.
"We have to find a common ground to deepen the dialogue and guarantee its continuation".
Sadiqi gave no further details and did not say when he expected the talks, last held in Abu Dhabi in 1995, to resume.

The UAE has urged Iran to agree to take the row to the International Court of Justice. Iran says its sovereignty over the islands is not negotiable but has called for bilateral talks with the UAE to clear up any "misunderstandings".
The two sides failed to resolve their dispute in their last meetings a year ago.

The UAE, member in the six-nation Gulf Cooperation Council -- also grouping the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman and Qatar, terms the Iranian presence on the islands as an "occupation" and deplores Iranian "measures to consolidate" it.
